rank_math_title: 2 Days Akagera Safari: Big Five Drives & Amazing Boat Cruise
rank_math_desc: 2 days Akagera safari from Kigali: a sunset boat cruise on Lake Ihema and a full-day Big Five game drive. Private 4x4, lodge, meals and park fees included.
post_content: This 2 days Akagera safari combines a sunset boat cruise on Lake Ihema with a full day of Big Five game drives, just 2.5 hours from Kigali.
overview:
This 2 days Akagera safari is the easiest way to see the wild savannah side of Rwanda. Akagera National Park lies about 2.5 hours east of Kigali and is now home to the Big Five, after lions and rhinos were brought back by African Parks and the Rwanda Development Board.

Day one ends with a sunset boat cruise on Lake Ihema. Day two is a full day of game drives across plains, woodland and lakeshore, in a private 4x4 with your own driver guide.

Why choose a 2 days Akagera safari?

Akagera is very different from the rainforests and volcanoes most visitors know Rwanda for. Here you find open grassland, acacia woodland, papyrus swamps and a chain of lakes, all in one compact park.

Two days is long enough to enjoy the lakes and the plains without rushing. It works well on its own, or as the wildlife part of a longer gorilla trip.

  • Big Five: lions, leopards, elephants, buffaloes and rhinos.
  • Water wildlife: hippos and crocodiles on the boat cruise.
  • Birding: more than 480 bird species recorded in the park.

What to expect on your 2 days Akagera safari

After pick-up in Kigali, you drive east through rolling countryside and check in at your lodge for lunch. In the late afternoon you board a boat on Lake Ihema. Hippos grunt in the shallows, crocodiles bask on the banks and fish eagles call overhead as the sun goes down.

Day two starts early, when animals are most active. You head north through the park looking for elephants, giraffes, zebras, topi and buffaloes, with a good chance of lions. A picnic lunch is served at a scenic spot before the drive back to Kigali.

Where you stay

You spend one night at a comfortable lodge in or near the park, on full board. Ask us about upgrades if you would like a tented camp or lakeside room.

Best time for an Akagera safari

The dry seasons, from June to September and December to February, are best for game viewing because animals gather near the lakes. The green season brings lush scenery, baby animals and excellent birding.

Only have one day? Try our Akagera day trip safari from Kigali. Want forest too? See the Akagera and Nyungwe safari. For official park facts, visit Visit Rwanda's Akagera National Park page.

faq.q: Is 2 days enough for Akagera National Park?
faq.a: Two days lets you enjoy a sunset boat cruise and a full-day game drive, which covers the park's main highlights. Add a third day if you want to explore the remote northern plains.

faq.q: What animals can you see on a Lake Ihema boat cruise?
faq.a: Expect hippos, Nile crocodiles, African fish eagles, kingfishers, cormorants and herons, plus elephants and buffaloes drinking along the shore.

faq.q: Does Akagera have the Big Five?
faq.a: Yes. Akagera is Rwanda's only Big Five park, with lions, leopards, elephants, buffaloes and black and white rhinos.

faq.q: How far is Akagera from Kigali?
faq.a: Akagera National Park is about 110 km east of Kigali, roughly a 2.5-hour drive.

faq.q: Can I add a night game drive to my 2 days Akagera safari?
faq.a: Yes. A guided night drive can be added at extra cost. It is a great way to look for leopards, hyenas, bushbabies and other nocturnal animals.

faq.q: Is an Akagera safari good for children?
faq.a: Yes. There is no minimum age for game drives or boat cruises, which makes Akagera a great family safari.

faq.q: What should I pack for Akagera?
faq.a: Pack light, neutral-coloured clothing, a warm layer for early mornings, a hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens.
